key_insight: Atmospheric plasma spraying produced predominantly crystalline Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings, with spray distance controlling the trade-off between mechanical performance and corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: A 90 mm spray distance offered the most favourable tested balance of hardness, wear resistance, and electrochemical behaviour.
method: Deposit low-glass-forming-ability Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 coatings by atmospheric plasma spraying at varying spray distances.
Characterize phase constitution, lamellar microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluate hardness, wear resistance, and electrochemical behaviour.
evidence_signal: XRD detected α-Fe(Si) and Fe–Zr intermetallic phases but no amorphous fraction; porosity ranged from 2.2% to 4.9%, while increasing spray distance improved hardness and wear resistance but reduced corrosion resistance.
watch_item: Treat 90 mm as the best condition among those tested, not a universal optimum; coating performance depends on particle thermal history and interlamellar defects.
paper_title: Phase Evolution and Structure–Property Relationships of Fe79Zr6Si14Cu1 Coatings with Low GFA Produced by Atmospheric Plasma Spraying
